subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should shared auto-reply delivery suppress an entire mixed payload when NO_REPLY appears as a trailing or own-line token, or keep the current behavior that strips the token and delivers substantive prefix text?
rationale: Current main contains both a narrower cron suppression fix and shared auto-reply tests that intentionally keep substantive trailing-token replies, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Suppress trailing silent acknowledgements
options.body: Treat own-line/trailing NO_REPLY as a whole-turn silent acknowledgement across shared delivery, while preserving non-trailing mentions and adding regression tests for direct replies and cron.

options.title: Keep current substantive-reply preservation
options.body: Document that only token-only, reasoning-prefixed, punctuation-wrapped, and cron-specific silent payloads suppress, while substantive prefix text remains deliverable after token stripping.

recommendation.title: Suppress trailing silent acknowledgements
recommendation.body: Treat own-line/trailing NO_REPLY as a whole-turn silent acknowledgement across shared delivery, while preserving non-trailing mentions and adding regression tests for direct replies and cron.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh is the current blame owner for the relevant token and final-reply normalization code on main.
